scoring.unit: per solo submission or shared team submission

questions.prompt: After Jesus finished instructing the twelve disciples, what did He do?
choices: He continued teaching and preaching in their cities
He stopped public ministry until the disciples returned
He returned to John the Baptist in prison
He gathered another twelve disciples
questions.correctAnswer: He continued teaching and preaching in their cities
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:1 states that Jesus continued to teach and preach after giving instructions to the twelve. He was sending them into a work He was already doing.
questions.application: Instruction is not the finish line. Where does what you have learned need to become obedience?

questions.prompt: What circumstance does Matthew identify immediately before John sends his question to Jesus?
choices: John was imprisoned
John was traveling with the twelve
John was preaching in Capernaum
John was speaking before the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: John was imprisoned
questions.explanation: John heard of Christ’s works while in prison. His question came in a real situation of confinement and unresolved expectation.
questions.application: What circumstance is putting pressure on how you interpret what God has already revealed?

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “Art thou he that should come, or do we look for □□□□?” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: another
questions.explanation: John sent his disciples to ask Jesus whether He was the Coming One or whether they should expect another. He took his question directly to Christ.
questions.application: When expectation and experience do not agree, take the question to Jesus rather than building a conclusion without Him.

questions.prompt: What did Jesus tell John’s messengers to report?
choices: The things they heard and saw
A new date for John’s release
A warning not to return to prison
A message about Herod’s political future
questions.correctAnswer: The things they heard and saw
questions.explanation: Jesus pointed to the evidence of His ministry: healing, restoration, resurrection, and gospel proclamation, in keeping with Isaiah’s witness.
questions.application: Measure your expectations against what Scripture reveals, rather than interpreting Christ only through what has not happened yet.

questions.prompt: Why did Jesus point John to the works people were hearing and seeing rather than promising John immediate release?
choices: His works testified to the identity and mission Scripture had promised
John needed to prove his loyalty before Jesus could respond
The crowds understood the Messiah better than John did
The Messiah would never confront suffering or injustice
questions.correctAnswer: His works testified to the identity and mission Scripture had promised
questions.explanation: The signs Jesus named were not random displays. They were consistent with the promised work of God (compare Isaiah 35:5–6 and 61:1). John was being directed to interpret his circumstances through revealed truth rather than require Jesus to follow an expected timetable.
questions.application: When God does not act on your preferred timetable, what does the evidence of Scripture still require you to believe and obey?

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be □□□□ in me.” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: offended
questions.explanation: Jesus called the hearer not to stumble over Him. John’s expectations concerning judgment did not exhaust the timing and breadth of the Messiah’s work.
questions.application: Can you release an expectation without walking away from Christ?

questions.prompt: After John’s messengers departed, how did Jesus identify John?
choices: A prophet, and more than a prophet
A reed shaken with the wind
A ruler dressed in soft clothing
A disciple who had abandoned his calling
questions.correctAnswer: A prophet, and more than a prophet
questions.explanation: Jesus upheld John’s prophetic calling, refusing to reduce his ministry to one question asked under pressure.
questions.application: Do not let one difficult moment erase a faithful history or cause you to misjudge someone else.

questions.prompt: What role did Jesus attribute to John the Baptist?
choices: The promised messenger who prepared the way
The priest who replaced the temple sacrifices
The king who would take Herod’s throne
The apostle who would lead the twelve
questions.correctAnswer: The promised messenger who prepared the way
questions.explanation: Jesus applied the messenger prophecy to John and connected John’s ministry with the Elijah-like role of preparing people for the Lord.
questions.application: God’s call to prepare a way is not the same as being the center of the work. Can you faithfully fulfill your role?

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “He that hath □□□□ to hear, let him hear.” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: ears
questions.explanation: Jesus closed this section with an invitation to receptive hearing. The issue is more than physical access to His words; it is willingness to receive them.
questions.application: What truth have you heard clearly but not yet received in a way that changes your response?

questions.prompt: What did the generation’s criticisms of both John and Jesus reveal?
choices: A refusal to receive truth, regardless of the messenger’s method
A disagreement between John’s message and Jesus’ message
A need for John to become less separated
A need for Jesus to stop eating with sinners
questions.correctAnswer: A refusal to receive truth, regardless of the messenger’s method
questions.explanation: They criticized John for his separation and Jesus for His fellowship. Opposite objections revealed the heart’s resistance, not a sound evaluation of truth.
questions.application: Have you ever rejected a correction because you disliked the messenger or the way it was delivered?

questions.section: A Generation That Would Not Respond
questions.prompt: In the context of criticism against both John and Jesus, what does “wisdom is justified of her children” teach?
choices: The outcome of God’s wisdom reveals its soundness despite inconsistent criticism
Every criticism of a religious teacher must be accepted as true
Wisdom is measured primarily by the approval of influential people
John’s message becomes invalid whenever people misunderstand his lifestyle
questions.correctAnswer: The outcome of God’s wisdom reveals its soundness despite inconsistent criticism
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:19 closes the contrast with a test of wisdom by what it produces. The response of the critics was inconsistent, but their reaction did not overturn the truth or fruit of what God was doing through John and Jesus.
questions.application: Are you judging truth only by how it is presented, or are you examining what it actually produces in obedience and repentance?

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “But wisdom is justified of her □□□□.” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: children
questions.explanation: Jesus concludes the comparison by saying that wisdom is vindicated by what it produces. The generation judged the messenger by its preferences.
questions.application: Look beyond the messenger’s style and examine whether the message and its fruit agree with Scripture.

questions.prompt: What response was missing in the cities where Jesus had done many mighty works?
choices: Repentance
Public admiration
Information about the miracles
Knowledge of the cities’ names
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance
questions.explanation: The text says Jesus rebuked the cities because they did not repent. Being exposed to His works had not produced the response required.
questions.application: Is there something you already know is true that still has not produced change in your life?

questions.prompt: Why is the comparison of Chorazin and Bethsaida with Tyre and Sidon so serious?
choices: The former cities had received greater revelation and were accountable for their response
The former cities were unaware of Christ’s ministry
Tyre and Sidon had never been subject to judgment
The cities were compared only because of their size
questions.correctAnswer: The former cities had received greater revelation and were accountable for their response
questions.explanation: Jesus ties the day of judgment to the light that people received. These cities had witnessed mighty works but did not repent.
questions.application: Ask not only what truth you possess, but how faithfully you are responding to the truth you have received.

questions.prompt: Why does Jesus compare Capernaum unfavorably with Sodom in the day of judgment?
choices: Capernaum received mighty works yet failed to respond in repentance
Capernaum had no opportunity to witness His ministry
Sodom had already received the same public works from Jesus
Capernaum was condemned because its buildings were larger
questions.correctAnswer: Capernaum received mighty works yet failed to respond in repentance
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:20–24 links greater exposure to the mighty works of Christ with greater accountability. Jesus teaches that responsibility is measured not merely by what someone has done, but by the revelation they have refused.
questions.application: What truth has been repeatedly made clear to you, yet has not produced a corresponding change in your life?

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “...hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto □□□□.” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: babes
questions.explanation: Jesus contrasted self-sufficient wisdom with receptive humility. The comparison focuses attention on the posture with which revelation is received.
questions.application: When Scripture confronts an assumption, are you willing to be taught?

questions.section: The Father Revealed in the Son
questions.prompt: According to Matthew 11:27, through whom is the Father revealed?
choices: The Son
John the Baptist
The rulers of the cities
Human wisdom by itself
questions.correctAnswer: The Son
questions.explanation: Jesus declared that no one knows the Father except the Son and the person to whom the Son reveals Him. God is made known in Jesus Christ.
questions.application: Allow the revelation of God in Christ to correct a preferred image of God rather than forcing Jesus into that image.

questions.prompt: To whom does Jesus direct His invitation, “Come unto me”?
choices: Those who labour and are heavy laden
Only those who already understand every doctrine
Only the disciples sent in Matthew 10
Only the inhabitants of Capernaum
questions.correctAnswer: Those who labour and are heavy laden
questions.explanation: Jesus personally calls the weary to Himself. His invitation follows the chapter’s warnings and teaching about revelation.
questions.application: Bring your weariness to Christ Himself instead of trying to resolve every burden by self-effort first.

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you □□□□.” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: rest
questions.explanation: Jesus promises rest to those who come to Him. The following verses make clear that this rest belongs to a life of learning from Him.
questions.application: What burden needs to be brought to Christ rather than managed entirely through your own control?

questions.prompt: Which sequence follows Jesus’ teaching about the way to His rest?
choices: Come to Him, take His yoke, learn of Him
Learn every answer, prove yourself, then come to Him
Avoid responsibility, leave the yoke, find a new master
First receive rest, then refuse any instruction
questions.correctAnswer: Come to Him, take His yoke, learn of Him
questions.explanation: Jesus says, “Come unto me,” “Take my yoke,” and “learn of me.” Rest is not the absence of discipleship but a life shaped by the right Master.
questions.application: Where are you asking Jesus to approve your own way rather than letting Him teach you His?

questions.prompt: What is missing from the claim that Jesus’ promise of rest means a disciple has no further responsibility?
choices: Jesus immediately calls people to take His yoke and learn from Him
Jesus limits His invitation to people who already know everything
Jesus says His rest is only for people without any burden
Jesus teaches that obedience is unnecessary once someone believes
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus immediately calls people to take His yoke and learn from Him
questions.explanation: The sequence in verses 28–30 matters: come, take, and learn. Christ offers relief from crushing burdens by bringing disciples into a new relationship under His instruction. His rest and His yoke belong together.
questions.application: Where do you want the relief Christ offers without accepting the direction His yoke requires?

questions.prompt: Complete the KJV wording: “For my yoke is easy, and my burden is □□□□.” (one word)
questions.correctAnswer: light
questions.explanation: Jesus completes His invitation by describing His yoke as easy and His burden as light. The promise is not absence of discipleship, but a life ordered under the right Master.
questions.application: Are you carrying responsibilities Christ actually assigned, or weight added by fear, performance, and the need for control?
